hoverDefinition: FCFF measures operating cash after taxes and reinvestment before debt service. In the stated simple build it is NOPAT plus non-cash depreciation, less capital expenditure and cash-linked operating working-capital growth.

covered: Operating cash perimeter, NOPAT bridge, depreciation/reinvestment, working-capital signs and financing exclusions.
deferred: Full tax/lease normalisation, acquisition adjustments, stock compensation, specialist financial businesses and complete professional FCFF estimation are deferred.

objectives.statement: Reconcile after-tax operating earnings to FCFF without including financing.
objectives.evidence: Use consistent non-cash and working-capital adjustments and interpret a decline in operating balances.

context.timeframe: Independent fictional teaching scenarios. Worked examples and practice start separately; they are not consecutive company-case rounds.
assumptions: Hypothetical operating tax is fully applicable/usable on the stated positive EBIT.
Depreciation is the only non-cash operating expense; working-capital changes are cash-linked and consistently defined.
Capital expenditure is cash acquisition spending. No other reinvestment, non-operating asset or cash adjustment.
Debt proceeds, principal repayment and interest are excluded from this FCFF perimeter; it is not necessarily reported operating cash.

framework.limitations: Conceptual teaching assumptions, with INR lakh as a unit rather than a jurisdiction. No tax rate, financing term, reporting classification, valuation input or management buffer is a current rule or market recommendation. Applicable framework, jurisdiction, reporting period and effective amendments require separate study.

mechanism.title: Define cash for all operating capital providers
paragraphs: FCFF is built before debt interest/principal service and after the reinvestment needed by the forecast operations. It therefore differs from cash available just to ordinary equity holders. A loan receipt can increase the bank balance without increasing FCFF.

Start with the specified after-tax operating earnings. For the simple positive-income assumption NOPAT = EBIT×(1−operating tax rate). Keep financing tax effects out of this operating build unless a consistent alternative method explicitly handles them.

mechanism.title: Bridge accounting earnings to cash after reinvestment
paragraphs: FCFF = NOPAT + depreciation − cash capital expenditure − cash-linked increase in operating working capital in these examples. Depreciation reverses a non-cash cost already inside EBIT; the actual asset payment still uses cash.

Working-capital growth absorbs cash, while a release contributes cash under the stated perimeter. Use either the defined net change or the component changes, not both. Remove non-cash measurement effects consistently before separately adding them back.

mechanism.title: Keep FCFF separate from a distribution promise
paragraphs: Positive FCFF does not prove the amount can be paid immediately to shareholders: debt service, restricted cash, timing and other claims remain relevant. Negative FCFF may reflect investment or operating weakness; interpret the cause and funding requirement.

Discount future FCFF at a rate matched to all capital-provider claims and risk. Do not add new borrowing as operating value or subtract debt service and then also apply the same enterprise-to-equity claims deduction without reconciling the chosen approach.

distinctions.name: FCFF and equity cash flow
distinctions.explanation: FCFF precedes debt service; equity cash follows a different claims perimeter.
distinctions.whenItMatters: Match the rate and valuation bridge.

distinctions.name: Depreciation and capital expenditure
distinctions.explanation: One is a non-cash allocation; the other is cash reinvestment.
distinctions.whenItMatters: Adding back one does not excuse omitting the other.

distinctions.name: Working-capital increase and release
distinctions.explanation: The period change determines absorption or release.
distinctions.whenItMatters: Use a consistent operating definition and cash-linked movement.

workedExample.setup: EBIT is 50 and the hypothetical operating tax rate 20%, fully usable. Depreciation 8 is already in EBIT. Cash capital expenditure is 18 and cash-linked operating working capital increases 6. Net borrowing 10 and interest 4 are listed for contrast and excluded from this FCFF build. No other adjustment exists.
steps: Add back depreciation 8 already deducted from EBIT: 40 + 8 = 48.
Subtract operating working-capital increase 6: unlevered operating cash in this build is 42.
Net borrowing 10 and interest 4 do not enter this before-debt-service operating cash perimeter.
Check the equivalent form: NOPAT 40 − net investment (18 − 8) 10 − working-capital increase 6 = 24.
workedExample.interpretation: The loan can fund cash needs, but it does not generate additional operating free cash flow.

statementEffects.explanation: Effects under the stated simplified scenario. Forecasts and economic values do not themselves create accounting entries.
changes: FCFF is an analytical cash-flow build, not a new entry or necessarily reported operating cash.
Specified operating profit, tax and reinvestment adjustments yield before-debt-service cash 24; financing settlement and complete company balances require separate data.

misconceptions.correction: Add back the non-cash charge once in the specified cash bridge.

practice.setup: Independent data: EBIT 32, hypothetical operating tax 25%, depreciation 4 already in EBIT, cash capex 10 and cash-linked operating working-capital increase 3. No other adjustment exists.
practice.question: What FCFF follows?

options.feedback: Depreciation already reduced EBIT and must be reversed once in the cash bridge.
A working-capital increase uses cash; it is not a receipt.

hints.text: Reconcile operating earnings, non-cash cost and the two reinvestment uses.

reflection.prompt: What assumptions make the working-capital adjustment valid?

practice.setup: Independent data: NOPAT 20, depreciation 3, cash capex 12 and a cash-linked operating working-capital decrease of 5. New net borrowing 9 is shown separately. There are no other adjustments.
practice.question: What FCFF follows before debt service?

options.feedback: The additional 9 is lender funding, not FCFF.
FCFF = 20 + 3 − 12 + 5 = 16. Net borrowing 9 is excluded. The same change entered as closing less opening is −5, so subtracting that change adds 5.
A working-capital release adds 5 instead of subtracting it.

practice.solution: FCFF = 20 + 3 − 12 + 5 = 16. Net borrowing 9 is excluded. The same change entered as closing less opening is −5, so subtracting that change adds 5.
